content: Erythema refers to the redness of the skin that occurs due to capillary congestion. This condition arises when capillaries dilate, leading to increased blood flow in the affected area, which manifests as redness. It can be triggered by various factors, including infections, physical manipulation such as massage, electrical treatments, acne medications, allergic reactions, physical exertion, exposure to solar radiation (e.g., sunburn), and hair removal methods like waxing or plucking. Erythema is a frequent side effect of radiotherapy, as ionizing radiation exposure during treatment can cause skin redness. Additionally, circumoral erythema (redness around the mouth) is recognized as a characteristic sign of acute oleander poisoning following ingestion. The causes of erythema are diverse and include conditions such as atopic dermatitis, chickenpox, contact dermatitis, fifth disease, hand-foot-mouth disease, impetigo, insect bites or stings, Kawasaki disease, lupus erythematosus, measles, psoriasis, roseola, rheumatoid arthritis, rubella, scarlet fever, seborrheic dermatitis, shingles, and perianal abscesses. Erythema can also be associated with specific conditions, including erythema ab igne, erythema annulare centrifugum, erythema chronicum figuratum, erythema migrans, erythema craquele, erythema dyschromicum perstans, erythema elevatum diutinum, erythema gyratum perstans, erythema gyratum repens, erythema induratum, erythema infectiosum, erythema marginatum, erythema multiforme, erythema nodosum, and erythema toxicum neonatorum. In approximately 30-50% of cases, the underlying cause of erythema remains unknown. Differentiating erythema from other skin conditions is essential, as many rash-like presentations can mimic erythema. These conditions must be considered in the differential diagnosis to ensure accurate identification and appropriate management.
